listings.prefix: Terry Allen & The Panhandle Mystery Band
listings.core: Bloodlines LP Fate Records 1983
listings.current_title: Terry Allen & The Panhandle Mystery Band Bloodlines LP Fate Records 1983
listings.description_original:
Terry Allen's third album, 1983, on Fate Records, Chicago, with the Panhandle
Mystery Band and Lloyd Maines. Includes "Gimme A Ride To Heaven Boy" and "Oui

sensibility, out of the Lubbock, Texas scene that also produced Joe Ely and
Jimmie Dale Gilmore.

listings.prefix: Terry Allen & The Panhandle Mystery Band
listings.core: Smokin' The Dummy LP Fate 2 1980
listings.current_title: Terry Allen & The Panhandle Mystery Band Smokin' The Dummy LP Fate 2 1980
listings.description_original:
Second album by the Texas songwriter, sculptor and visual artist Terry Allen,
released 1980 on his own Fate Records out of Chicago (catalogue Fate 2).
Backed by the Panhandle Mystery Band with Lloyd Maines on pedal steel. PRC-
Richmond pressing. First pressings shipped with a lyrics insert. Allen's
catalogue reached a far wider audience after Paradise of Bachelors reissued
this album in 2022, and the original Fate pressings are the ones collectors
look for.

listings.core: Maiden Voyage LP Blue Note BST 84195 1985 DMM Reissue Jazz
listings.current_title: Herbie Hancock Maiden Voyage LP Blue Note BST 84195 1985 DMM Reissue Jazz
listings.description_original:
Herbie Hancock's 1965 Blue Note classic, with "Maiden Voyage", "Dolphin Dance"
and "Little One", recorded with Freddie Hubbard, George Coleman, Ron Carter
and Tony Williams. This copy is the 1985 Direct Metal Mastering reissue,
identified by the runout stamp BST 84195 DA 21, the DMM logo on the label, and
the printed Michael Cuscuna "Blue Note Story" inner sleeve. Pressed by Pathe
Marconi EMI in France. This is a reissue, not a 1965 original.

listings.core: 60 Years Of Music America Hates Best LP Liberty LMP 3154 1960 Mono
listings.current_title: Spike Jones 60 Years Of Music America Hates Best LP Liberty LMP 3154 1960 Mono
listings.description_original:
Spike Jones novelty and comedy LP on Liberty Records, 1960, mono pressing.
Jones and his City Slickers built a career on demolishing popular songs with
gunshots, cowbells and gargling, and were among the biggest-selling comedy
acts of their era. Please note: there is an ink signature on the rear cover.
It is offered unauthenticated and is not represented as genuine; photographs
are included so buyers can judge for themselves.

listings.core: Apnea White Label 12" Techno Minimal House Electronic Promo
listings.current_title: Geoff White Apnea White Label 12" Techno Minimal House Electronic Promo
listings.description_original:
White-label twelve-inch by Geoff White, the American techno and minimal house
producer whose work has appeared on Ghostly International, Background Records,
Anodyne and Context, and who also records under aliases including Aeroc. The
sleeve is hand-marked "Apnea". The specific release is not confirmed, since no
title of that name appears on his published discography, so "Apnea" may be a
track title or a label reference. Buyers who know the catalogue are invited to
check the runout matrix.

record, valued for the depth and presence of its hall sound.

listings.core: Sound-System LP Columbia FC 39478 1984 Bill Laswell Grammy
listings.current_title: Herbie Hancock Sound-System LP Columbia FC 39478 1984 Bill Laswell Grammy
listings.description_original:
Released August 1984 on Columbia (FC 39478), the follow-up to Future Shock.
Produced with Bill Laswell, featuring Wayne Shorter on soprano saxophone,
Foday Musa Suso on kora and Grand Mixer D.ST on turntables. It won the Grammy
for Best R&B Instrumental Performance, Hancock's second consecutive award in
that category after "Rockit". Includes "Junku", written for the 1984 Los
Angeles Olympics.

first ceremony held. The record is widely credited with opening the commercial
folk revival of the following decade.

listings.description_original:
Soundtrack to the 1959 Samuel Goldwyn film of the Gershwin opera, on Columbia
Masterworks (OS 2016) in a gatefold jacket. The film was later withdrawn from
circulation by the Gershwin estate and has never had a general home-video
release, which keeps steady interest in the soundtrack as the most accessible
record of the production.

listings.core: Meet The Best In The West Bar None LP RCA PRM-194 Country Promo RCA Victor
listings.current_title: Meet The Best In The West Bar None LP RCA PRM-194 Country Promo RCA Victor
listings.description_original: RCA Victor Special Collector's Edition country compilation (PRM-194), issued as a promotional pressing rather than for general retail sale. Features The Browns (“The Three Bells”), Floyd Cramer (“On the Rebound”), Skeeter Davis and Bobby Bare (“A Dear John Letter”), Don Gibson (“Give Myself a Party”), Hank Locklin (“Foreign Love”), Roger Miller (“You Don't Want My Love”), Jim Reeves (“Four Walls”), Mack Sanders (“Long Distance”), Hank Snow (“I'm Movin' On”), and Dottie West (“Here Comes My Baby”). Promotional country samplers of this period carry their own following among collectors of the label.
